title: Planar magnetic drivers
summary: A thin diaphragm carries conductors within a magnetic field.
explanation: Current in the diaphragm’s conductors interacts with the magnetic field to move the sound-producing surface. Audeze describes distributing driving force across the diaphragm.
decision: Compare the actual model’s sensitivity, impedance, weight and documented power requirements. Driver technology is one selection criterion.
limitations: A manufacturer’s claimed superiority is not an independent result. Planar construction does not by itself establish better sound.

sources.title: Audeze: planar magnetic technology
sources.scope: Supports the stated facts; not independent performance testing.

title: Dynamic drivers
summary: A voice coil drives a diaphragm in a magnetic field.
explanation: An electrical audio signal passes through the coil attached to the diaphragm; the resulting motion creates sound.
decision: Use model-specific measurements and compatibility information when available. A driver family alone does not predict tuning or comfort.
limitations: The cited manufacturer contrasts its own planar technology with dynamic designs. We use the mechanism explanation, not its competitive sound-quality claims.

sources.title: Audeze: dynamic and planar mechanisms
sources.scope: Supports the stated facts; not independent performance testing.

title: Open-back headphones
summary: An enclosure design, distinct from the driver technology.
explanation: Open-back headphones have an acoustically open rear enclosure. Sennheiser’s HD 414 is a documented 1968 milestone in this design history.
decision: Editorial guidance: consider a quiet listening room and check sound leakage before using headphones near a recording microphone.
limitations: Open-back does not mean planar, and it does not establish a particular frequency response or a universal sound-quality advantage.

sources.title: Sennheiser: Our history

title: Active noise cancellation
summary: Microphones and electronics generate a signal that reduces unwanted sound.
explanation: Bose describes sensing surrounding noise and producing an opposing signal. This active process differs from a physical seal that passively attenuates sound.
decision: Editorial guidance: confirm ANC explicitly in the model specification. Check fit and the manufacturer’s battery conditions before choosing for travel.
limitations: An ANC label does not quantify attenuation or establish hearing protection. A microphone used for calls alone is not proof of ANC.

sources.title: Bose: what is active noise cancellation
sources.scope: Supports the stated facts; not independent performance testing.

title: Bluetooth LE Audio
summary: A Bluetooth Low Energy audio architecture, not a synonym for all Bluetooth audio.
explanation: Bluetooth SIG’s LE Audio suite includes LC3 and multi-stream audio. It builds on core capabilities introduced with Bluetooth 5.2.
decision: Check explicit support on both the source and the headphones, including software requirements.
limitations: A Bluetooth 5.2 or later label is insufficient evidence of LE Audio support. No catalogue model is automatically tagged from its version number.
